vern hallucination and long-session drift.
# dsh-outer-brain
English | 中文
**A philosopher's way of thinking, made executable — dialectics and practice-testing instead of prom
pt-level discipline. Built to govern two things that get worse the longer an agent runs: hallucinati
on and long-session drift.**
Most tools try to make the model *smarter*. This one doesn't. It gives the agent:
- **a way to think** — find the principal contradiction, refuse false dichotomies, let practice rath

er than rehearsal settle a claim;
- **a way to check itself** — a ledger, executable criteria, and o
utside review, so "done" is a fact rather than an assertion.
## Two failure modes, and why length makes them worse
An agent is bad at catching itself doing either of these:
| What goes wrong | How it shows up | What governs it |
| **Hallucination** | The ledger turns green and the summary reads well, but the deliverable does no
t exist. "Last time it was like this." "The conditions aren't right so I can't." | Criteria must **a
ctually run a command and read the exit code**; evidence without a **receipt** (verbatim command / p
ath / URL) carries zero weight; after the machine gate passes, a **jury of three non-communicating r

eviewers** rules by majority |
| **Long-session drift** | Twenty turns in, the agent is optimising s
omething nobody asked for, or re-running the same command while calling it progress | The **contradi
ction tree** keeps the principal contradiction pinned so it cannot quietly migrate; `stalled` catche
s semantic circling while `spin` catches mechanical repetition (OR-ed together); overturned claims a
re **recorded** instead of silently forgotten |
## Install
### Option A — Desktop app (most users)
Open **Settings → Plugins**, find `dsh-outer-brain`, enable it.
### Option B — CLI profile (`web`, `tui`, …)

> ⚠️ **This command alone does NOT mount the plugin.** `dsh plugin` forwards its arguments verbatim
to pnpm — it only adds the package to that profile's `dependencies`. **Mounting is decided by `dsh.p
adds the package to that profile's `dependencies`. **Mounting is decided by `dsh.profile.bundles`.**
You must also add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Without the `bundles` entry, the package installs cleanly, **nothing runs, and no error is raised**
— it will look like the plugin is broken.
Then restart DSH.
> **It starts silent.** Say **"开机制"** (turn the mechanism on) to activate it, **"关机制"** to dismiss i
t. That is deliberate — a tool for catching bad work should not be watching you all the time.
## The 12 tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `brain_task` | Declare the task: your words + my reading of them + why this approach + the result

I want |
| `brain_plan` | Delivery ledger: milestones, artifacts, **executable criteria**, definitio

ns (is / not / limit) |
| `brain_verify` | Run the criteria (the mechanism really executes the comma

nd and reads the exit code) + convene the jury automatically |
| `brain_contra` | Contradiction tree

: two paths reaching the same endpoint with different results (Φ≠0), with eight disposal moves |
| `
brain_observe` | Evidence pool: claim / prior / expectation / observation / receipt, scored by likel

ihood ratio |
| `brain_settle` | End-of-round settlement: water level into history, hazards closed o

ut, off-contract observations captured |
| `brain_status` | Current water level, alarms, outstanding

debts |
| `brain_lift_check` | Lift criteria: is a proposed lift a real take, a fixation, or simply

not liftable yet |
| `brain_dissolve` | Lift receipt: what became of the contradiction that was sup

posed to be resolved (dissolved / transformed / still there) — **see known limitations** |
| `brain_

escalate` | Escalate: what I need / why I cannot do it myself / where I would resume from |
| `brain
_terminate` | Termination declaration: achieved (list verifiable facts) / unreachable (name the miss

ing condition) / redirected |
| `brain_boundary` | The mechanism's own boundaries: register the wall
s the mechanism itself ran into |
## Configuration
Most behavior is tunable in `cordis.patch.yml`. The key settings:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The state file defaults to **DSH's working directory** (`process.cwd()`), which means a `.outer-brai
n-diag.log` and state JSON appear next to wherever DSH was started. Set `workDir` in `cordis.patch.y
ml` to pin them to a fixed location:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Known limitations (0.1.0)
Three paths in this release do not work end to end. They are listed here rather than hidden, because
the whole point of this plugin is that **advertised capabilities should exist**.
| Area | What breaks |
| `brain_dissolve` | Resolves the id against the task/question tree instead of the contradiction tre
e, so passing a contradiction id (e.g. `C0`) reports "node not found". Lift receipts cannot be close

d through this tool in 0.1.0. |
| Unknown pool | `brain_settle` captures off-contract observations,
but nothing is wired to `classify` / `absorb` / `reject` them. If any stay open past the water line,

"achieved" becomes permanently unreachable. |
| `brain_terminate` | `blocked_evidence` is validated
and echoed in the receipt, but is not persisted onto the milestone record. |
## Honest limits
- **This is an early 0.1.0 mechanism**, designed for single-machine personal use. It is not a substi

tute for a mature workflow.
- It **injects a system prompt** into your session and **intercepts some

"done" claims**. That is how it works, not a side effect. Say "关机制" at any time to turn it off.
- T
he jury needs a model that supports structured output; a small `maxTokens` truncates verdicts, which

looks like "vague criteria" but is really "the output never finished".
- The mechanism has its own
defect history. One failure mode kept recurring during development: **the function was written, the
unit test passed, but nobody called it** — it computed numbers that never reached a decision. Each c
ase was fixed, and it proves one thing: **a tool can stop you from fooling yourself; it cannot stop
ixed, and it proves one thing: **a tool can stop you from fooling yourself; it cannot stop itself.**
